title: indigo_mount_synscan: publish the coordinates from the position poll through indigo_update_coordinates() like the other mount drivers
description:
Owner request (2026-11-19), first step of the work started in ticket 42b85be0-1f19-4607-b3c3-746e60317d17. The owner's rule: the systemic way for a mount driver to publish coordinates from its position poll is indigo_update_coordinates(); a driver that does not use it is defective.

Current state (indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver, 3.0.0.23): the driver never calls indigo_update_coordinates(). synscan_read_mount_coordinates() computes the horizontal coordinates and MOUNT_LST_TIME itself, and synscan_update_mount_coordinates() (called from the poll and the guider finalizers) sets the states and publishes MOUNT_RAW_COORDINATES, MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES, MOUNT_SIDE_OF_PIER and the rest with indigo_update_property(). The other mount drivers (ioptron, lx200, nexstar, nexstaraux, pmc8, rainbow, starbook, temma, simulator) set the equatorial values and state and call indigo_update_coordinates(device, NULL), which derives MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES and MOUNT_LST_TIME and publishes them together with MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES.

Change: make the poll path of mount_synscan publish MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES, MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES and MOUNT_LST_TIME through indigo_update_coordinates() and remove the driver's own duplicate computation and publication of those properties where the library function provides them; keep the driver-specific properties (MOUNT_RAW_COORDINATES, MOUNT_SIDE_OF_PIER, MOUNT_STATE, X_ENCODER_POSITION) as they are. Driver version incremented; .driver edited and outputs regenerated.

Scope limits: no change of indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c and no change of which state the poll publishes (the poll still sets OK/BUSY as today; keeping an ALERT of a refused request is a later step). No change of published coordinate values is intended.

Verification: before changing behaviour, run one identical scenario (home position, GoTo on both sides of the pier, tracking, both hemispheres, and the alt-az operating mode if the simulator supports it) against the driver built from master and from the change and compare every published value and state of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES, MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES, MOUNT_LST_TIME and MOUNT_RAW_COORDINATES; report any difference (for example horizontal coordinates derived from the alignment-corrected pointing versus from the published equatorial coordinates) instead of hiding it. Simulator suite updated where the publication order or count is asserted; recorded runs with tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan and, when the mount is available and power-cycled in its home position, --hw; MIGRATION_STATUS.md counts updated.

outcome.summary:
Reviewed 9d41dfae9..HEAD (mount_synscan 3.0.0.23 -> 24, test, MIGRATION_STATUS). No blocking defects.
Verified: (1) Callers: poll, autohome/park/home/goto finalizers and synscan_wait_axis_stopped all go through synscan_update_mount_coordinates(), which resolves device->master_device before indigo_update_coordinates() and returns before it when !IS_CONNECTED, so MOUNT_* context is always the mount's; connect path calls only synscan_read_mount_coordinates(), and indigo_mount_change_property(CONNECTION) derives HOR from the freshly read EQ before defining it, then the generated handler queues mount_timer_callback at once (LST stale only between define and that first poll, owner-accepted). (2) No driver code reads MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_* or MOUNT_LST_TIME_ITEM values for decisions; GoTo/park/home/side-of-pier use indigo_lst(NULL) or axis positions; the driver accepts no HOR requests. (3) States: library copies EQ state to HOR when HOR and GEOGRAPHIC are visible, same as the removed code; failed-read path (on_timer -> synscan_set_coordinate_state ALERT for EQ+HOR, LST not published) and connect ALERT path are unchanged. Hidden HOR now still gets LST updated (previously LST value froze) - an improvement. (4) synscan_de2h removed, no remaining references; its math equals indigo_radec_to_altaz (no refraction). (5) Regenerating the .driver with the worktree build/bin/indigo_generator in a temp dir gives .c/.h/_main.c byte-identical to the checked-in files. (6) New case passes 3/3 alone (20-21 polls, 18-19 with HOR, 13-14 with LST, 0 value errors); built against the pre-change .c (9d41dfae9) it fails (0 polls with HOR before EQ, 20 disagreeing). LST whole-second matching is exact-double against indigo_lst over a 3 s window, deterministic. Full synscan simulator suite run once: 104/104 PASS; test-clean done. (7) MIGRATION_STATUS 104 / 21 matches 104 registered simulator cases and 21 hardware cases. Version bumped in .driver and DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000018. No README, PROPERTIES or Xc

Verified: git diff 83d067eae 710604924 -- indigo_drivers/mount_synscan indigo_libs/indigo_align.c indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c indigo_test/integration/test_mount_simulator.c is empty; every file changed only by this branch equals 83d067eae and every file changed only by the parent equals 32e3954d2 in the merge; only MIGRATION_STATUS.md and TEST_SUMMARY.md were changed by both sides. No conflict markers in the merge tree. MIGRATION_STATUS rows: mount_rainbow 40 / 0, mount_simulator 29 / 0, mount_starbook 27 / 0, mount_synscan 104 / 21 equal the registered cases (40 in test_mount_rainbow_simulator.c, 29 in test_mount_simulator.c (non-benchmark main), 27 in test_mount_starbook_simulator.c, 104 in test_mount_synscan_simulator.c, 21 in hardware/test_mount_synscan_hw.c). indigo_libs, the mount_synscan driver (Makefile.drv) and test_mount_synscan_simulator build without errors or warnings on the merged tree; test-clean done. The earlier code-review findings for 83d067eae still apply unchanged (pass, two non-blocking remarks). Note only: TEST_SUMMARY's mount_simulator row (29 / 28 Failed, 2026-11-19 22:35) comes from this branch's already merged sub-ticket 29c486f3, not from the conflict resolution.

history.text: Building library in worktree for the master-vs-change comparison harness
Running the master-vs-change comparison scenario on the synscan simulator (both in parallel)
Stopped before finalising: comparison found az 0->360 at the north pole and a stale LST define at first connect

The version comparison on the simulator (master driver vs the change, same scenario) shows identical states, side of pier, equatorial and raw coordinates, and alt/az equal to 1e-12 deg, with these differences from publishing through indigo_update_coordinates(): (1) azimuth at the north pole (home position) is published as 360.000000 instead of 0.000000, because the driver's own conversion snapped |az| < 2 arcsec to 0 and the library does not (master already alternates 360/0 there: the library publishes 360 at connect and on a site change, the poll 0); (2) MOUNT_LST_TIME is defined with a stale value (0 on the first connect) and corrected by an update inside the same connection handler, as in every other driver on the library path; (3) the order of updates per poll changes from RAW, EQ, SIDE_OF_PIER, HOR, LST to RAW, SIDE_OF_PIER, HOR, LST, EQ. Accept the library behaviour and finish the ticket (A), keep a private LST assignment in the driver (B), or fix the two points in indigo_mount_driver.c in a separate ticket first (C)?

Owner (2026-11-19): azimuth 360 at the pole is a defect, it has to be 0. To be fixed in the library conversion in its own ticket, for all drivers; this ticket continues after that fix so that the synscan poll publishes 0 through indigo_update_coordinates(). The MOUNT_LST_TIME value defined at connect is not decided yet.

2026-11-19: the library azimuth fix (sub-ticket 29c486f3, due north published as 0) is merged into this ticket's branch. The recorded simulator run of mount_synscan is made in the owner-ordered final recorded run of all mount drivers at the end of the series, not separately here.

Non-blocking remarks: (a) EQ is computed from the LST of the read, LST/HOR from time(NULL) at publish; if a second boundary falls between them HOR/LST lag EQ by 1 s of hour angle (~15 arcsec). Library-wide behaviour shared by every mount driver using indigo_update_coordinates(), within the owner's accepted scope. (b) Test: the update hook is installed before the latitude change to 48; a poll whose RAW publish starts after the hook and computes HOR before the latitude write (microsecond window) would be flagged as a value error. Installing the hook after wait_for_number_item_value() would remove that theoretical race.
